title: MethylRAD: a simple and scalable method for genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using methylation-dependent restriction enzymes
boundary: Methylation-dependent Mrr-family cleavage generates short methylated-site-centered tags for direct adapter ligation, PCR and gel-selected libraries. This positive modified-base-directed fragment preparation differs from bisulfite conversion, methyl-CpG affinity capture and HELP/Methyl-MAPS methylation-sensitive routes. FspEI is the defining example; named alternative Mrr enzymes and tissue/species applications are not extra methods.

title: G4access identifies G-quadruplexes and their associations with open chromatin and imprinting control regions
boundary: Native-chromatin nuclease digestion enriches protected G4-associated DNA for sequencing without antibody capture or crosslinking. This physical enrichment frontend differs from registered G4-seq polymerase-stalling observations on extracted DNA and ordinary nucleosome-fragment readout. Nuclease enrichment does not prove exclusive recovery of folded G4 molecules; cell types and ligand treatments remain one method.

title: Topoisomerase IIβ targets DNA crossovers formed between distant homologous sites to induce chromatin opening
boundary: Etoposide-trapped topoIIbeta complexes are antibody-selected while retaining covalently linked G-segments and associated T-segments. High-salt fractionation distinguishes these physical fractions; an adapter-mediated chimera branch links segments from the same complex. This differs from registered CC-seq antigen-independent covalent-complex enrichment/TDP2 end tagging. eTIPa/eTIPb remain complementary branches of one candidate; topo species, neuronal treatments and read analysis do not add methods.
